correctness.rationale: Finite m6 gives a mean-square second derivative with Gaussian increment variance bounded by m6 times the squared separation. Kolmogorov continuity and integration give a C² version. Bulinskaya's lemma applies to X' (its one-point Gaussian density is uniformly bounded), so critical points on compact intervals are simple. Rice gives J using independence of X' and X'' by evenness of the covariance. The disjoint open two-mesh intervals around strict lattice peaks each contain an interior continuous maximum; the two end effects disappear in the expected intensity. For V=1-r(h)>0 the comparison differences have correlation (1-2r(h)+r(2h))/(2V), giving the stated arccos formula including perfect correlations by continuity. For u=(4V-V(2h))/(2V), u=(m4/(2m2))h²[1+(m4/(12m2)-m6/(6m4))h²+o(h²)]; the square-root and arccos corrections combine to the stated coefficient. Its numerator is m2² times the variance of ω² under the derivative-energy law. In the bandlimit range the arccos input is the mean of cos(hω) under the (1-cos(hω))-weighted spectral law. This law is a decreasing positive tilt, in ω², of the derivative-energy law, so its mean ω² does not increase. Strict convexity of cos(h sqrt(x)) on [0,Ω²] (sin z-z cos z>0 for 0<z≤π) gives strict Jensen unless ω² is constant there. The tilt preserves nonzero spectral support. For one absolute frequency the formula gives p_h=hω*/(2π) through hω*=π, including the perfect-correlation endpoint. A zero-frequency atom has no effect.
residual_risks: Finite-mesh converse was checked only under the stated bandlimit and mesh bound; no claim for larger meshes or weaker regularity. Packaged numerical tests are supplementary.
